speaker: The Chairman
text: Please take your three cuts together, Mr Zaqy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I believe, for instance, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) can play a driving role to energise the sectors in helping SMEs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I hope that both the Ministry and IMDA will look into how it can help with industry transformation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For one, it can address the feedback from industry about technology adoption and, secondly, it can also help SMEs better leverage the grants available to help them transform.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I would also like to know what could possibly be done to catalyse a quicker adoption of technology, such as the Internet of Things and data analytics, among SMEs, which can consequentially provide better insights into their business, workforce and improved customer service.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This goes beyond the current capability of SME Centres or industry associations because the largest impact will come from deep experts who can identify trends, intellectual property (IP) and research that can drive innovation at all levels − the businesses, across the value chains and the whole ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Given how technology is strategic to Singapore's future, I believe that expert access to our business and technology know-how will be crucial to the success of our SMEs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I urge the Ministry to consider all of these questions so that our home-grown companies can maximise the opportunities presented to them by digital disruption.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Given the disruptive and rapidly evolving nature of the digital economy, how can we ensure that we also retain our technical expertise to remain and provide projects and create an ecosystem that continually challenges them?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Without opportunities to progress careers with technical depth, many ICT professionals switch to general management and into sales to further their careers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Thus, the industry may keep losing skilled resources and not grow deep skills as a whole.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In identifying the need to build a vibrant ecosystem, what steps can the Ministry take to reduce our over-reliance on foreign, migratory talent in this area and build genuine career opportunities for Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is important that for us to have a healthy, sustainable and vibrant digital economy, that we have an ecosystem which must provide opportunities for exciting technical career paths.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will help us drive innovation and cutting-edge tech application and research.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is one of the reasons why ecosystems, such as those in San Francisco, thrive as hubs of innovation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I look forward to hearing the Ministry's plans on these initiatives.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, with cybersecurity being of increasing importance in a digital economy, what is the Ministry doing to increase its cybersecurity capabilities, as well as to strengthen the cybersecurity industry in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Last year, the Government announced that it will separate its networks from the Internet.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What is the feedback from civil servants and public servants thus far?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Has there been impact on customer service from the Government by those agencies that have been affected by this policy?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Has the Ministry studied the impact on the productivity and effectiveness of knowledge workers in the agencies and their responsiveness to the public?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is inevitable that the more exposed we become to the virtual world in a digital economy, we are exposed to more and more risks and trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will need to study and assess these negative effects so that we would not be caught off-guard.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Today, the topic I wish to discuss is how to drive SMEs' digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Later this month, the Chamber's office will be relocating to the Trade Association (TA) Hub in Jurong East.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: More than 20 TAs will come on board with us.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The TA Hub will be the base from which we shall be promoting the digitalisation of enterprises.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: We have specially set up the TA Committee to help industry associations integrate resources, improve capabilities, promote collaboration amongst TAs, build up partnership relations and provide a platform to channel feedback to Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: One of the important areas of the TA Committee's work is to help local enterprises go digital.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Making digitalisation a reality involves two factors: one is system and the other is workers.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: SCCCI's subsidiary, the Singapore Chinese Chamber Institute of Business, will be doing its best to help TAs train their workers.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: But the other challenge of promoting digitalisation is how to apply a standardised system to improve the effectiveness of the whole industry.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In the interconnected Internet world, companies need to plug into a collaborative network.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The effectiveness of digital technology could only be evident if the system is compatible with that of your customers, suppliers and partners.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: If not, the transfer of large masses of data could cause system errors.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Such programming defects that occur willy-nilly could frustrate SMEs and make them lose faith.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Applying a standardised system for the industry is likened to learning a common language to facilitate communication.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, many food and beverage (F&B) establishments are using the electronic menu ordering system.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Customers who frequent different restaurants first need to study how to use their systems.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: After being accustomed to Restaurant A's system, you need to start over again with Restaurant B.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Starting from the menu selection, serving of food to paying the bill, the entire process is fully automated.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Businesses could even use the data captured to analyse which dishes are the most popular and decide on the quantity of ingredients to purchase.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: But from a deeper perspective, if every restaurant uses its own system, we could never standardise the employee training curriculum.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Moreover, whether customers can get used to the system would determine their continued patronage.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: If F&B players use a common system, the entire process of customer acceptance could be accelerated.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This simple example allows me to clarify that in the journey of digitalisation, TAs and industry associations must consider the big picture of the whole industry, including problems which may be encountered by related industries.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: They should not digitalise for the sake of doing so.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, please take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That is the question I have for the first cut.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In particular, how is the use of consumers' data, such as their purchase habits and feedback, to be utilised more optimally by SMEs and companies so that they may evolve their products and services to better cater to current needs?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Ministry also be looking at ensuring that the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) remains relevant?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We are now in a climate where we are encouraging companies to use data innovatively and optimise business opportunities, yet the personal data in their possession needs to remain secure and protected, which makes it a bit more difficult for their businesses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am pleased to note from the Budget that the Government is helping businesses to go digital and encouraging the use of digital technologies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Indeed, this is a step in the right direction towards a more productive and technology-savvy workforce.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am keen to hear about MCI's detailed plans and strategies to build a digital-ready workforce.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Furthermore, how does IMDA plan to develop a future-ready media workforce?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It has been over two years since PDPA was implemented.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With more companies taking their businesses onto different platforms, there is a greater exchange of customer information, particularly online and through social media.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the past, email addresses and phone numbers were among the main concerns of consumers who were receiving spam emails and messages.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Now, with social media having a greater role in transactions and information exchange, data protection has become more complicated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Furthermore, recent high-profile hacking incidents have led to the accidental compromise of customer and personal information, showing the vulnerability of online data systems.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: First, to provide an update on the implementation of PDPA.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: As a result, lots of personal data are vulnerable to abuse and cyberattacks.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Similar breaches had also previously happened in private firms, such as K- Box and PropNex Realty, in which the personal data of thousands of customers were leaked online.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Thus, the personal data of Singaporeans are at risk of abuse.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This will undoubtedly be a cause of concern for consumers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Smart Nation envisions a Singapore where citizens are empowered by technology to live meaningful and fulfilling lives.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Such efforts will also include providing greater access to official statistics and information on official programmes under Public Service initiatives.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In raising this cut, I use the word "smart" in Smart Nation with a non-digital definition in mind.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: At a time when poor information, misunderstanding and even misinformation and fake news are becoming increasingly prevalent, efforts that assist and allow the public access to primary sources of information so as to have an informed fact-based public debate are especially needed.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This allows a discerning active citizenry to participate in governance and have a direct stake in policy-based discussions with fact and reasoned opinion as the order of the day, as opposed to wild diatribe and unsubstantiated exaggerations.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: No doubt, the latter will not be easy to filter out, given the open nature of the Internet and the information age we are in today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Government has stated that it is looking at how it can reinforce its legal and regulatory hands against purveyors of falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But the long arm of the law alone is unlikely to engender a Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Smart Nation must, at its core, understand where to find news that allow its citizenry to make informed decisions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Parliament is an important if not central conduit for information dissemination and can make a seminal difference.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For Singaporeans to be resistant to fake news, it must be sufficiently informed, and providing a "live" and open Parliamentary platform could serve as a key inoculant against fake news.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Educating the public about their rights and responsibilities as citizens and voters are equally important and useful next steps.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The digital revolution has opened many doors to provide such services competitively.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In fact, it was noteworthy that the recent Budget speech delivered by Minister Heng was streamed "live" and available on The Straits Times' website.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The absence of full Parliamentary question and answer clips and Second Readings of Bills appears contrary to the principles of open Government.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: No doubt, the delayed Channel NewsAsia (CNA) videos available online shortly after a Parliamentary session are a notable improvement from the past.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I also note that the scope and length of coverage have increased progressively as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, current reports on Parliamentary proceedings by the mainstream media centre on snippets sometimes omit key statements, facts and context, and this depends on the liberty of editors.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As a written record of speeches, there are also limitations as to what the Hansard can convey in a timely manner, given society's migration to video-based formats on our smart phones.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Ministry can review its position on this matter and consider bringing "live" Parliamentary proceedings in full to our smart devices, in step with our evolution as a Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: To my surprise, it seems that installing a speed camera is not so straightforward.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This made me wonder whether the Government can do more to tap on technology to deliver its services to the public.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For example, we currently already have closed circuit television (CCTVs) to monitor places where there is illegal parking.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also urge the Government to consider using the latest camera technology to curb high-rise littering and littering along areas like public parks or bus stops and other busy public places.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Government can use sensor technology to track whether roads and drains have been regularly cleaned by the cleaning companies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Today, when my mobile data usage on my phone reaches 80% of my limit, Singtel automatically sends me a short message service (SMS) to alert me.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can the Government rely on such similar technology to alert residents when their household water usage exceeds 80% of the norm?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will remind residents to be more careful about their water usage.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: This calls to mind the bigger issues of the growing risk of losing access to essential Government services for groups of Singaporeans in the face of digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Let us try to make our pioneering Smart Nation even more inclusive.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Other than to promote reading, the libraries can also double up as community hubs that support the adoption of IT and lifelong learning, as well as being the point of access to e-Government services.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As the Government continues to digitise more and more of its services, it is crucial that those who are unfamiliar with IT be provided with a public channel that they can use to transact with the Government.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given that both NLB and the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) are under the purview of MCI, both agencies could work closely to ensure that dedicated and secure terminals are made available in public libraries to those who have no home access to the Internet so that they can access e-Government services.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Furthermore, NLB can value-add to this service by using it as a platform to enhance community engagement.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Specifically, could NLB perhaps engage Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) students from relevant IT courses in the Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs) or polytechnics as volunteers to provide onsite assistance to residents who need help with their e-Government transactions?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that this is something that the Government can consider.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Sun Xueling, please take your three cuts together.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Digitalisation is a challenge as well as an opportunity for SMEs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While it significantly changes how business is being done, disintermediating the middleman and impacting companies that may be asset-heavy, it also offers an opportunity that SMEs can scale up and internationalise quickly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If they are able to successfully leverage on digitalisation, there is a real chance of us being able to break out of the constraints of land and rental, manpower and small home markets, achieving higher revenue, higher productivity and lower manpower reliance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we encourage our SMEs to embark on digitalisation and what holds them back?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One of the reasons for the slow adoption of digitalisation could be a lack of familiarity with technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One way of increasing awareness of digitalisation for SMEs could be to organise meet-the-firm sessions, akin to a Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS), except that instead of meeting a Member of Parliament to seek assistance and introduce the various Government schemes, the firm and its management can meet an IMDA officer to be introduced to various digitalisation options.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For it to be impactful, the outreach should look to touch base with as many firms as possible, but provide solutions targeted to each firm's technology capability level.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There is a tipping point for technology, where a critical mass of users starts using digital solutions, digitalisation could undergo an exponential adoption rate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Let us help to initiate a tipping point.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Data can help power services to ensure seamless operability to the advantage of Government and local enterprises.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: GovTech is leading the Government's efforts to embrace digital transformation and innovate to enhance Public Service delivery.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How has it enabled the Government to better harness ICT and related engineering to drive transformation and innovation amongst other Government agencies?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While data is being provided to the public to engage in co-creation of applications, what is being done to systematically integrate new applications to existing Government services to provide users a one-stop user-friendly experience?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Lastly, as more Government services are migrating to e-services, how are we enabling our seniors to keep up with the changes?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This could be done in the form of simple workshops conducted by volunteers at void decks for seniors or at community hubs, such as town hubs and libraries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our seniors need a personal touch to encourage them to use e-services, and there should be more one-on-one opportunities for them to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Theories abound about how fake news and push-through reporting were alleged to have had a hand in shaping voter behaviour during Brexit and the recent United States (US) Presidential Elections.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Countries, such as Germany, are looking at laws targeting fake news while Internet and the social media giants, Google and Facebook, are reviewing their policies to curb the spread of fake news.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Minister Yaacob Ibrahim had shared that the Ministry plans to amend both the Films Act and the Broadcasting Act this year to take into account changes in technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given media convergence, amendments to the Broadcasting Act is likely to be a dominant media legislation.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This poses a number of challenges for the regulation of content.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For me, there are two components to this new challenge: firstly, that content creation is now global and, secondly, that most content is distributed via huge and powerful global platforms.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The distribution of content has become easier and anybody can create content and have it go viral.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In "the good old days", content was stored in physical media, and copying and distributing it took much effort.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The current situation is complicated by the fact that content is now global.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Content providers do not need any sort of physical presence in Singapore to serve content to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They do not even need to have a formal website per se, as their content can be spread virally through Facebook or other social media.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How does the Ministry intend to create some form of parity between local and overseas content producers?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What about foreign content creators using Singapore as a base to create and distribute content that may be sensitive to our neighbours?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The next challenge is that most consumers will discover that the content they receive will come through either Facebook or Google, or might be even sent through WhatsApp, which is also a subsidiary of Facebook.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The very size and scope of these platforms give them significant power in discussions with any individual government.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: There is very little that a government can do to compel them to act, short of banning their services within the country.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, the loss of access would create a huge uproar.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given the vast amount of content that is uploaded to these sites, it would be unreasonable to expect them to police them constantly.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A more pertinent question is whether they are obligated to remove "objectionable" content once it is flagged to them.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Again, this is a difficult task, for what is objectionable to one may not be to another.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It sometimes seems that there are people on the Internet whose sole purpose is to get outraged by one thing or another.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, we cannot just pander to the lowest common denominator.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Or even if this law gets passed, this is not without challenges.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The term originated to describe sites that manufactured stories out of thin air to drive clicks and profits.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The term is now being used rather loosely, even by senior officials, to describe news and opinions that do not comply to their liking.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I think we can all agree that completely fabricated stories with no basis in reality should be clamped down with all the tools that we have.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, the world is a messy place and facts may not be easy to agree upon.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Take one example − the prosecution and defence lawyers in a murder case will use the facts to spin completely different narratives.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In effect, only one of those two narratives is real and the other is, by definition, "fake".

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Would news outlets presenting and supporting the case for the defence be denounced as fake news by the prosecution and vice versa?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What if we load the stakes and say that the case involves the murder of a prominent religious leader, which has the potential to stoke religious tension?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Would there be pressure to stop media outlets and social media sites carrying reports supporting the defence team's arguments, even though they may ultimately prove to be correct?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A totally draconian approach is unlikely to work.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It would also harm our image as an open society and a great place to live and work, and contradict our long-standing light touch regulatory regime.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As the furore over alleged fake news in the United States (US) shows, even a mature democracy can be rocked by such threats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ours continues to be an important role moving forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CFE laid out the opportunities and challenges in the next phase of our economic development, and the Budget detailed how we can thrive in this exciting future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One way is to harness technology to seize the opportunities in the digital economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have always leveraged technology to overcome our constraints.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, several years ago, we decided to lay fibre optic cables and improve mobile speeds across the island.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our huge investments in infrastructure now give us vast connectivity across the nation and beyond.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: That connectivity has opened up a new space for Singaporeans, presenting many opportunities for businesses and work, research and learning, social interactions and self-expression.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It enables us to leverage infocomm media (ICM) technologies to transform the way we live, work and play.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MCI, Madam, has also contributed to the use of technology in other sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the video, you saw a GovTech Technology Associate share how his team used data science to identify the cause of the Circle Line breakdowns last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are many more examples of how GovTech supports national objectives through technology, such as in developing smarter Government digital services or developing platforms, such as a National Digital ID system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We thus have the building blocks for Singapore to thrive in a much more technologically-enabled world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Yet, for all their possibilities, these new spaces and technologies have also raised concerns about their impact on jobs and equality, and about their potential to dehumanise society and corrode our values.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As a society, we need to apply a critical eye to the implementation and use of new technologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Together, we need to define the rules by which this new space works so that it optimises opportunities, fosters innovation, ingenuity and creativity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But, most importantly, to do so in a way that will strengthen our communities and improve our lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Cognisant of these challenges and concerns, MCI undertook three key steps in 2016 to help Singapore better prepare for the digital economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This allows us to better utilise our resources and allowed convergence on changes necessary for our digital transformation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Cyber Security Agency (CSA) will also take steps to elucidate cybersecurity so that everyone understands the importance of cybersecurity and how they, too, can play a role in securing our IT systems from cyberattacks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thirdly, Madam, MCI is building and developing an ecosystem that enables our businesses and people to thrive in a digital economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In chairing the TeSA Governing Council, IMDA leads a diverse range of stakeholders to realise this vision, including companies, TAs and Government partners, such as SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In tandem with this focus on training, we also created physical spaces, like Pixel Labs, to help our young and startup community gain a foothold in the digital economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And we will continue to consult and partner our TAs and businesses to help companies adopt ICM technologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will build on these foundations in 2017 and beyond.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In line with CFE to keep Singapore's economy competitive and position our country for the future, we plan to, first, help companies transform and build strong digital capabilities, second, deepen our workers' technical expertise and, finally, continue to digitalise the Government to better serve Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A number of Members have asked how we plan to help SMEs transform themselves digitally and prepare for the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We strongly believe that digital technology can help companies across all sectors drive productivity, create growth, catalyse innovation and boost competitiveness.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, let me elaborate on two examples that illustrate how companies have used digital solutions to improve their business under IMDA's iSPRINT programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The system allows teachers to take attendance via iPad, instantly generate students' progress reports with an e-portfolio, and keeps parents updated on students' activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This not only helped free up teachers to devote more time on their students' development and well-being but also improved communication between parents and the school.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thus, building on iSPRINT, IMDA and CSA will work with agencies, such as the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING), with an "SMEs Go Digital" programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It will help raise SMEs' overall level of digital readiness by giving them step-by-step advice on the technologies to use at each stage of their digital journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For those with more advanced needs, such as data analytics and cybersecurity, experts at a new SME Digital Tech Hub will provide dedicated assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides advice, the hub will also help connect SMEs to ICT vendors and consultants, as well as conduct workshops and seminars to help build SMEs' digital capabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And for any progressive SMEs interested in experimenting with emerging digital technologies, they can pilot co-creation projects with IMDA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA can also connect SMEs to experts to help them in their innovation expertise, as suggested by Mr Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Playing the role of Chief Information Officer, IMDA will synergise these plans across different sectors, including ensuring interoperability, as suggested by Mr Thomas Chua.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, ICT companies can not only identify areas their solutions can potentially value-add, but also whether they can be deployed to other sectors with similar needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Similarly, SMEs can be guided on how different solutions, such as cybersecurity, data analytics and e-payment, can be integrated together to meet their requirements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For a start, we will focus on sectors where technology can uplift productivity, such as retail, logistics, food services and cleaning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Through SMEs Go Digital, IMDA will collaborate with big corporations who can play an influential role in helping to digitalise the SMEs they work with.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These large companies are well-placed to help uplift the entire sectors, by pushing the mass adoption of impactful digital solutions to SMEs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One example, Madam, is Robinson's, a big retailer which uses an e-procurement platform to transact electronically with their 200 SME suppliers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Furthermore, as Robinson's could provide suppliers with their daily sales data, the system allowed both parties to benefit from better planning and inventory management.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Market leaders, such as telecommunications companies (telcos) and banks, can also work with ICT companies to expand their traditional services and provide more value-added solutions to their SME customers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Starhub will partner IMDA and various vendors to provide F&B and Retail SMEs with a comprehensive digital solution package.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This includes bundling existing broadband and wi-fi connectivity with a suite of complementary solutions, such as digital ordering and payment, digital advertising, cybersecurity and retail analytics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Sandwich outlet Toasties has already adopted Getz' solution, while another four merchants, including the popular Al-Azhar Restaurant, are being engaged as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I appreciate Members' support for the programme, but note potential concerns about its implementation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I also agree with Mr Thomas Chua's point about Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Recognising the SMEs' digital needs vary widely across and within sectors, we will invite TACs, other key industry players and SMEs themselves to provide feedback, create awareness and help to improve SMEs Go Digital.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our main aim is to ensure it meets the needs of SMEs and remains "user-friendly".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This means rolling out an integrated approach to groom local ICM companies by expanding Accreditation@IMDA and introducing other schemes to grow these companies and build an innovative ecosystem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Accreditation@IMDA is a key initiative for promising local tech startups, as it provides resources and investments to help them build a track record and accelerate growth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Accredited in December 2015, it is now working with agencies, such as the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and Public Utilities Board (PUB) to explore using its unmanned aerial vehicles in maintenance and inspection work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In urbanised Singapore, AeroLion's technology assist agencies in navigating challenging environments to better detect problems like building cracks and debris.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The results gathered from AeroLion's analytical data also helps staff devise potential preventive measures and run our main infrastructure systems more efficiently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Accreditation@IMDA was initially launched to leverage Government demand to identify and establish the credentials of promising startups.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thus, for larger high-growth ICM SMEs which require targeted intervention to scale overseas, we plan to help them partner LLEs and MNCs, such as CapitaLand, Mediacorp and Sentosa Development Corporation, for product innovation, capability building and export to overseas markets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, in the area of the Internet-of-Things, IMDA will work with CapitaLand to develop the smart building capabilities of these Singapore tech companies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CapitaLand's global network of over 500 properties offers these companies a living lab for ideas and prototypes to be field-tested and validated, supporting the co-development of globally competitive breakthrough technology solutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This applies to both the ICM sector and digital-related work across all industries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At last year's COS, I announced TeSA would pioneer new ways of enabling Singaporeans to acquire ICT expertise and skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am pleased to report the progress TeSA has made.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hakim Ariffin, 26 years old whom you saw earlier came from a finance background and has since successfully converted to a programmer employed with American healthcare firm Merck, Sharpe & Dohme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Lim Yi-Min, 23 years old, is now a Data Scientist at National Computer Systems (NCS).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Through the TeSA's company-led training (CLT) programme, she was able to better transition from school and a degree in engineering to a working environment and a new exciting world of data analytics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A seasoned veteran with 30 years' experience in systems administration and technical support, Alvin challenged himself to pursue a new career in cybersecurity after being laid off.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Going forward, Madam, we will continually expand TeSA's range of training partners and courses, as well as look at new initiatives to drive Singapore's ICT skills landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Beyond ICT professionals, it is important for the workforce of other sectors to start digitalising.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) aims to develop the next generation of business leaders, helping aspiring Singaporeans acquire leadership competencies and critical experiences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: TeSA will work with LDI and other partners to implement on-the-job training leadership programmes with a focus on developing tech management skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This complements other programmes supported by TeSA, such as Squared Online for Singapore SMEs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A digital leadership and marketing course, it was developed in partnership with Google to help SME leaders and employees who are keen to digitalise their businesses and navigate the evolving digital landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue to develop a capable, future-ready workforce in other ways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA has developed a Media Manpower Plan which Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will share later.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will also continue working closely with tertiary and pre-tertiary institutions to boost our pipeline of talent.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One programme is Industry Preparation for Pre-graduates (iPREP) which equips pre-graduates with relevant industry-ready skillsets and work experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One beneficiary is Jaren Lim, an undergraduate from the Singapore Management University's (SMU's) School of Information Systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Jaren is passionate about IT and interested in how organisations function.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Through iPREP, he now better understands how technical expertise marries with business acumen, before he enters the workforce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This means our businesses, people and Government must all play a part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Singapore has always embraced technology to serve our needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I recall we formed the National Computer Board in the 1980s to computerise the Civil Service and improve public administration services through the use of ICT.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In a similar vein, the Government will take the lead in Singapore's whole-of-nation initiative to develop into a Smart Nation, with GovTech helping to lead digital transformation within the public sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the past year, GovTech has been developing national-level digital platforms and infrastructure to help catalyse the digital economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech has also partnered other agencies to use technology to enhance and transform the way Government services are delivered to our citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate more on their work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Also, as Singapore transitions into a digital economy, more and more aspects of our everyday life will be made digital.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In today's landscape, we recognise that cyber threats have been increasing in frequency, scale and sophistication as governments, businesses and consumers have become more reliant on information systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Government is aware that it is a potential target.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thus, as Singapore's Cybersecurity Strategy coordinates our efforts to build a resilient and trusted cyber environment, the Government has already taken the necessary steps within the Public Service to strengthen our systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To further reply Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Miss Cheng Li Hui, the Internet Surfing Separation policy is meant to protect Government systems and citizens' data by removing one avenue which cyberattackers can use to steal information.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides setting up the necessary infrastructure to ensure officers can still easily access the Internet for work, we are adjusting and adapting our work processes and introducing productivity solutions and tools to help maintain an efficient and productive Public Service.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There has been no impact on our public service delivery.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Members of the public are still able to send and receive emails from Government offices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Government digital services and transactions by the public and businesses have also been unaffected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are working to ensure a smooth transition for public officers to meet our target May 2017 implementation date.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This separation, Madam, is necessary and we will continue to review and calibrate our security measures to ensure our systems remain resilient and trusted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Protecting Singapore's cyberspace and Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) remains a core mandate of CSA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Cyber defence is now part of Total Defence, so the National Service (NS) cyber vocation announcement by MINDEF is timely.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is an important part of the overall national strategy to build up a skilled workforce, with full-time National Servicemen (NSFs) being deployed to CSA to augment capacities in protecting our CIIs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are already growing our talent pipeline through upskilling and reskilling programmes under TeSA and the Cyber Security Associates and Technologists (CSAT) programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Armed with their NS cybersecurity experience, some NSFs may choose to take up careers in Government agencies, such as CSA, MINDEF and GovTech, while others will enter the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They will not only strengthen the wider cybersecurity ecosystem but also become future cybersecurity entrepreneurs creating jobs and economic growth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As part of the ongoing efforts to professionalise the wider cyber workforce, the scheme will also provide a framework to catalyse growth and uplift the overall industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am likewise pleased to see the industry playing its part in growing the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Singtel, for instance, is reaching out to students through an interactive online portal called the Cyber Security Experience (CSX).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This portal will be launched soon and, hopefully, such efforts will interest students to explore cybersecurity further and eventually join this exciting field.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would now like to reply to Ms Sun Xueling and Mr Ong Teng Koon on how we will be updating Singapore's media regulations to better keep pace with technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I had previously spoken about our plans to update the Films Act, which was enacted back when screening a film required a physical copy on a reel.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, films can be directly streamed from overseas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will be updating the Films Act for this digital age.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Singaporeans now have access to a wide variety of content on the Internet and are no longer limited to services offered by Mediacorp or our subscription TV operators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: When overseas content providers are directly targeting Singaporeans, we need to ensure that their content is in line with our community values, including the need to uphold racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are studying this carefully to make sure that any changes we make will not add undue burden to our businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In reviewing our amendments to BA, we will rationalise some of the changes made in past years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Many Members have spoken about the increased dangers of fake news.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But if an entity reports news about Singapore regularly to inform Singaporeans on matters of public interest, we expect them to do so responsibly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I am heartened that industry giants like Facebook and Google have realised that some control is necessary in this environment where misinformation can spread so easily.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Google has prohibited advertisements on sites with deliberate misinformation while Facebook is mobilising users to call out misinformation in their news feeds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Yet, even as we update our legislation and regulations, it is even more important that those who use, create and share content on the Internet do so safely and responsibly, while being discerning on any information they find online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To this end, we will continue to promote information and media literacy to all Singaporeans, particularly our young and those who may be vulnerable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, Madam, to summarise, the digital economy is coming.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It will create growth, jobs and higher wages for Singaporeans, but will also require us to adapt and be open to many changes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: My colleagues will continue to share MCI's plans to help Singaporeans prepare for the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Amongst others, Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on how we will enable Singapore for the digital age, capitalising on data and technology, while Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will share on our initiatives to support the media sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, Madam, it is our businesses and people who must be willing to take advantage of these opportunities, making the effort to relearn, upskill and keep pace with technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The opportunities for economic success are here and waiting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We just need to have the initiative to seize it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Each time, we bounced back stronger, more resilient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must be equally adaptable in this time of disruptive technology and innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Fortunately, we start from a position of strength.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have never been more highly skilled, more globally reputable and more digitally connected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How then will we deal with the very real anxieties expressed by Singaporeans and Members of this House in this time of disruption?

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thirdly, we will help our people seize opportunities in the digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government will take the lead in Singapore's efforts to build a Smart Nation, and I thank Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Ms Sun Xueling for their questions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Indeed, we will innovate with technology and data to deliver better public services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, to develop national platforms which make it easier for individuals to access services, and also for the Government and businesses to deliver those services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example is the Smart Nation Platform, which GovTech is working to enhance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This common sensor and communications platform facilitate the collection and sharing of data across the island by multiple agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through the Smart Nation Platform, large amounts of data will be generated by a variety of agencies through a wide mix of sensors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These can yield meaningful analysis and applications for the Government to better deliver key public services, such as transport, utilities and much, much more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Citizens can also be much better informed and make better decisions through the applications and the data analytics available, often through their personal mobile devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The next area that GovTech will play a leading role in is to build capabilities, such as data analytics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Sun Xueling asked about how GovTech has led the Government's efforts to embrace innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One recent example was in solving the Circle Line breakdowns last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Data scientists from GovTech solved the problem through a very innovative application of data science.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The full details are available on their blog.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The value of data we hold is enormous, especially when correlations can be drawn between datasets, rather than just analysing a dataset on its own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This was so in the example of the Circle Line, where the specific rogue train was identified by correlating video footage of train movements to data on breakdowns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, the video footage was originally collected for very different purposes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is the case for much of data; sometimes we are not aware of the full utility possible at the time of collection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we want to enable data to be shared across domains and agencies so that we can harness the greater value of data and unlock a greater future potential from the data.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, GovTech will use technology to deliver anticipatory, integrated, data-driven, well-designed digital services, predictive services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The public can "Ask Jamie" questions using natural language.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: You can ask questions and get answers instantly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Using algorithms, it searches through data and gets better over time as the public asks it more questions and refines the way in which it interacts with the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would encourage Members to try out the service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: GovTech is also looking at how messaging platforms, such as Facebook Messenger, can be used to perform transactions with "Ask Jamie", for example, to register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) for an overseas trip.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is possible that in the near future, engaging Government services will be as simple and as convenient as messaging a friend.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This digital transformation of Government will rest on the right expertise and talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: GovTech has and will continue to take the lead to build ICT and related engineering capability in the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Mr Zaqy Mohamad that an ecosystem must provide opportunities for cutting-edge tech application and research.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To become a truly Smart Nation, the Government cannot be the only player.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Industry and academia must come together to develop deep capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We do not know what skills will be needed in 10 years' time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we must come together across these different domains − Government, industry, academia, private enterprise − and work together to ensure that we are resilient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have the infrastructure in place to support a digital economy, and an immense amount of digital activity is already happening here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This means that businesses have all the tools they need to participate effectively in the digital economy at the higher end of the value chain here in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, many companies lack the awareness of the possibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In particular, with data science, companies cite a lack of good data, awareness, expertise and some concerns about regulatory clarity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad's question on how we can drive quicker adoption of technology, such as data analytics, is extremely relevant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: DIPO will address industry concerns by facilitating data-driven innovation projects and the development of the data ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Data Sandbox will also provide data analytics tools to help companies build expertise in data science.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To encourage co-creation of solutions using data by citizens and businesses, GovTech has been actively improving data.gov.sg, focusing on quality, instead of only quantity, of data.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, a Developers' portal was introduced last year to provide data users and developers easier access to real-time data via application programming interfaces (APIs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: DIPO will also work with Government agencies to release more economically-useful data through data.gov.sg.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I encourage Members to investigate that uniform resource locator (URL) as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Central to this is the trust that citizens have about the use of their data.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As companies innovate with data, we also want to make sure they know how they may use personal data, in accordance with regulations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is increasingly important with the rising use of smartphone apps and e-commerce websites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The PDPA has been implemented for over two years now and we have seen greater awareness among organisations of the need to protect the personal data in their possession.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: PDPC is also committed to improving the data protection ecosystem and will put in place additional measures to ensure businesses know how they may use personal data responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is important, Madam, that everyone has a chance to participate in the digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are committed to making it easier to access Government digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Currently, we have trained staff at 27 Citizen Connect Centres island-wide to assist less tech-savvy users in accessing Government digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At these Citizen Connect Centres, you can perform many Government digital services, such as requesting for your Central Provident Fund (CPF) statement, applying or renewing Housing and Development Board (HDB)/Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) season parking tickets, online registration for SingPass and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is important that we enable our seniors to keep up with these changes and, hopefully, become IT-independent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One way we are doing so is through the Intergen IT Bootcamps and the Silver IT Fest Mass IT workshops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through these, IMDA has been collaborating with primary to tertiary-level schools to provide opportunities for the younger and older generations to come together and learn about IT.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Seniors can also learn about IT at any of the 29 Silver Infocomm Junctions and People's Association's Senior Academy Centres available island-wide where affordable and customised IT classes are available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA will continue collaborations with schools and organisations and regularly review the curriculum to ensure seniors are equipped with applicable skills, such as using social media apps and accessing Government digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Interested youths can sign up to be Friends of Silver Infocomm volunteers to help seniors at such events and participate in the Silver IT Fest classes as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Given our libraries enjoy a wide reach among our citizens, they can also play a bigger role in the future in assisting citizens with Government digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are other ways to support more families in benefiting from connectivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We also partner private sector organisations in these efforts, such as the Post Office Savings Bank (POSB), the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) FairPrice Foundation and NetLink Trust.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I hope that among these types of outreach efforts and the examples provided by some of the members about volunteerism for our young, that more organisations and more youth volunteers will step forward and come on board to work with us to make sure that everybody in Singapore has an opportunity to participate in the digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But this is not something only for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Disruption is here and companies are already transforming to respond to it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has applied natural language processing and machine learning technology in an innovative way to analyse corporate financial data and unstructured text from public domains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Its programme fuses this data together with their clients' own database to provide strategic intelligence that their clients can use to make decisions about their strategic investments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And it can do so in a shorter amount of time and get better and sharper all the time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But DC Frontiers itself has faced an internal disruption.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This willingness to be reskilled and to keep learning has become part of the company's ethos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, now, when they hire someone into their company − and they are still hiring, despite this disruption – they are looking at the skillsets of that person not just for the job they have been hired for, but considering whether two to three years from now, that this person is suitable and adaptable to being reskilled and redeployed into a new vocation and job.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is about six years old and has gone international with offices overseas and clients across borders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is not a startup anymore, although it behaves like a startup through an attitude of bringing people in with a willingness to disrupt themselves, their business models and internal work processes, and redeploy both themselves and their workers going forward, and making that part of the company's ethos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: DC Frontiers has retained the startup mentality even as they have scaled up and gone international.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a very useful mental model, a frame of mind for us as a nation and as we deal with digital disruption and consider the possibilities ahead of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But it is not just about our national effort, it is not just about a single company's efforts to be disruptive and innovative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It goes all the way down to the individuals and the opportunities they have here in Singapore today, and not just the Singapore of tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In order to use an app like this to transcribe natural language, you would need to hold the phone with a microphone close to your mouth so that your speech is captured clearly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As the text is transcribed, it comes out on the phone, the right way up for you, the speaker.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As such, it is upside down for the person you are facing, the hearing-impaired person that you are trying to translate to.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, what you have to do is to pass the phone back and forth, which interrupts the flow of conversation and makes it not an enabler, but a disruptor to the conversation you are trying to have between a hearing-impaired person and someone who is not.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Very simply, it is a natural language processing engine which flips the text upside down, so you can keep it there, by your mouth, and you can have a conversation back and forth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It seems like a very simple design change, but it is very useful and has been used regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The disruption, innovation and ideas are here today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We cannot be planning for something in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are here right now and we need to be active and proactive about embracing the opportunities that are available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we have never shied away from a challenge to seize opportunities and deliver results.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Rather than see threats and disruption, we must continue to see the world through the eyes of a startup, full of promise and full of opportunity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Similarly, we need to be committed to keep learning, trying and striving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is with that attitude, and with the Government, businesses and people coming together, that we will become the best place in the world to incubate the next big change, a Smart Nation at the leading edge of the digital technology revolution.

speaker: Mdm Speaker

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What outcomes have we seen and can expect to see with the increased funding?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, our younger generation are consuming children's programming from the Internet.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Even on our national channels, many of the programmes for children are from western cartoons, which may not necessarily be aligned to our Asian values system.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While we have done better in documentaries, current affairs shows and primetime local programmes, the Ministry can do more to develop high quality local children's programmes that can engage our children better, which will also bring about better learning outcomes of our local environment, cultures and values.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Overall, while we often speak about quality programming, quantity also matters, to ensure sufficient local content to provide more choices for different segments and tastes among our older and younger generations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I hope the Government will continue to find ways to expand our PSB space as new Internet-based media platforms continue to grow.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Can PSB stay relevant and continue to evolve and meet the changing consumption habits of Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On one hand, it is easy to blame the Internet for taking away audiences from our national television medium.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is worthwhile transforming our approach to engage and work with the mainstream and digital channels and review the ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Their locally produced content continues to maintain viewership ratings on the television medium.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is also attributed to the fact that they have quality content in look and feel but, more important, with storylines that connect with local and international audiences, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Moving on to newspapers, many news agencies globally have struggled for readership, competing with digital channels.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our newspapers have always played an important role to uphold quality journalism and reporting while also fulfilling the important role of an enabler for national communications.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have seen some consolidation as readership declines, and this is more concerning for the minority language papers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: How can the Ministry enable and support our print media to face the challenges of the era of digital news, to uphold professional journalism in the era of sensational news, flick baits and alternative facts, and help uplift their digital capabilities to better reach out to and engage the digital generation?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These include loans, private equity and crowdfunding, with film production completion bonds being used to help independent filmmakers secure funding from these kinds of sources.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, are there tax incentives for private investors who fund movie productions?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is IMDA supporting the development of a crowdfunding industry for films?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such efforts may not only help commercially oriented funding but also encourage private funders to step forward to finance films for which they have a passion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A better financial ecosystem for film production in Singapore would place the industry on a more sustainable footing.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Unleashing private funding will also help the cause of artistically or nationally important films that may be less commercially viable.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would also like to know how IMDA is supporting local filmmakers to offer content online, as this is a fastest growing platform for film consumption.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: All these are important for the quest to create more Singapore movies that can inspire us and help bring the light of Singapore to the world.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: MCI tackled the impact of convergence head-on by realigning itself to face the challenges thrown up by disruption.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This restructure is critical in the evolution of our media landscape and our collective Smart Nation ambitions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Already, we have seen a slew of measures that include the creation of thousands of jobs in the ICT sector, the launch of the 2025 Design Masterplan, strengthening of our cybersecurity sector and the digitisation of Government services, just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: As such, I am very heartened and appreciative of MCI's various measures to support the freelance community.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These measures, which include the setting up of a portal to assist in job matching, will definitely help the sector, given the slowing economy.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: However, I do feel that the freelance community itself needs to be more proactive to take advantage of these initiatives.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I urge the community to put aside their individual interests and come together as a community, so that the entire ecosystem can benefit from these measures.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: But I feel more can be done to broaden the skillsets to fully benefit from the impressive infrastructure we have at Mediapolis @ one-north.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: In some sectors, there seems to be a disconnect between the talent available and industry needs.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
