speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we look at what we have now and our sense is that it is meeting the needs of what Mr Singh had spoken about in his speech.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The provision of the information is out there, timely and comprehensive, and organised in a manner which is easy for viewing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If you put up the whole "live" stream, someone who is viewing it has to sit from the beginning to the end.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Whereas the way Mediacorp does it, they arrange it by date and then by the speakers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is actually a lot easier for someone to find what he or she wants to look for in a convenient way.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We believe that this format will fulfil the objectives and the benefits that Mr Singh spoke about.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is something which I think we will look at whether there are further ways that we can improve.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The archival period, for example, as I mentioned in the past, used to be one month, and it was lengthened to six months.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I support some of the Members who are asking for this streaming.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is not just about watching the archival.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I think it is the whole process of how this Parliamentary debate is being done.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This is very important in our political education, especially for the people.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: That is why I would like to advocate for it to be done.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I wonder whether the Government would actually consider multilingual productions, especially for the narrative kind of productions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: What we have now is, a lot of time, what we see on TV, especially narrative stories, it looks as if they appear in a very weird world whereby the Chinese gather together and talk about their own stories, and Malay content.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I think we need to have multilingual content so that we are used to serving different languages, so that it does not become a kind of a myth that we live in, whereby we all live in our own different language worlds.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, I just want to ask the Minister of State if he can share with us the survey that was done where he said that the people are more satisfied with the content in the newspapers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: When he said they were more satisfied, what does it mean?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: What is the comparative study that we are talking about, as in "more satisfied"?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, I just want to know, in terms of the reading habits, whether we are reading more literature − I am talking about narratives like prose, poems and novels − or are we reading more of those do-it-yourself (DIY) toolkits kind of books?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I was checking with Minister Yaacob whether he wants me to answer all the questions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I will answer the first three questions and the Minister will answer the fourth one.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If I may, I will start with the last question.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is the Media and Consumers Experience Study that is done by IMDA.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, they improved from sixth place to first place.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I recognise this is just one dimension, one key performance indicator, one study, which is why we need to really look at what are the ways to further work with our media partners to help them to build capabilities and develop good content.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That, ultimately, is what the people are looking for.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is found already in different productions but it is whether we can help to develop the content further and for such shows to be more commonly found.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is where the Member is coming from because it is actually already available in some productions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I think the Member's question is whether we think this can be done further.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will certainly discuss with Mediacorp and also what I had mentioned in my speech, the independent producers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because not everything has to be done by Mediacorp.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: A lot of good productions can be done by Mediacorp, by independent producers or collaborations between Mediacorp and the independent producers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have the elderly and the young, we have the families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If Members notice carefully, in the last few years, we basically moved our library to be more thematic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If you want to read something on early childhood, for example, Jurong Library is the place to go.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have also created spaces so that we can attract certain segments of the population.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Pasir Ris Library was redesigned to attract younger people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, now, they are coming in and they are not only reading, they are learning together, they are co-creating content.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the Library that is about to open in Sengkang, we have a section called the "Tween" section.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is somewhere in between the teens and the young kids, where they come in, they want to read books of their choice, at the same time, they want to have a certain ambience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we cater to all segments of the society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The other thing that we observed, for example, is that our e-books are becoming very popular.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is very difficult for us to decide which genre because it depends on the number of e-books that we can acquire.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have to acquire these books from the people that produce them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: You can see, if you go down to the e-books section, some of the books that are extremely popular are, for example, some of the current non-friction books which are hitting the New York list of bestsellers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There is no clear dominant genre, but we want to encourage reading, no matter what books that you like to read, and to read consistently and constantly.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Mr Chairman, just a quick point of clarification to Minister of State Chee regarding the issue of "live" Parliamentary broadcasts.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Minister of State alluded to the fact that someone looking at a "live" broadcast may not know what exactly he or she is looking at, whereas if you look at the video clips that have been uploaded, then those can be clearly labelled and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Does the Minister of State not recognise that that issue can be addressed by placing a single crawler on the screen to state who is speaking and what they are speaking about and what is the context.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: That is what we see on C-SPAN, for example, in the US.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Would the Minister of State also not recognise that such "live" broadcasts could be done via a web platform rather than through the TV, and that could be very cost-effective?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Leon Perera for his questions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I did not mean to say that a person who is watching the "live" streaming or broadcast would not know what was going on.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because Mr Pritam Singh was talking about "live" streaming, and if you put "live" streaming on the Internet, somebody watching it would have to watch the whole proceedings.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Whereas if you were to organise it in the way the CNA microsite currently does, which is, they separate it, sort it by date, and then by name of the Member of Parliament, it is easier from the point of view of the public who is going in to view the clips that he or she wants to view.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: You do not have to sift through the whole proceedings to look for what you are interested in and just play those few minutes of the clip that you want to watch.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that was what I meant in terms of the convenience for the viewer.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To answer the Member's second point, we do recognise, as in my response to Mr Pritam Singh, that this issue has pros and cons.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Pritam Singh also agrees with me that there are pros and cons.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think the Minister of State has not addressed my concern about it being a whole of political as well as the political learning process, especially knowing how the legislative process is being done.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: As someone who actually comes into this Parliament fresh and new, I realised that it was a lot of things for me to learn in this process.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, that is why watching it through the whole process will be very important.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Chairman, just now when we were having our debate, we see students coming in and that is actually part of the education process as well, to expose our young people to what is going on in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is also available for any member of the public who wants to come in and watch, not just "live" broadcast but "live".

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I agree with Mr Kok that it is useful for people to understand what Parliament has discussed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is a point which I also made in my speech.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is useful for people to understand the debate, the points that are being made, but this information is available on the online Hansard, the full set of information and all the videos, speeches, questions and answers are also available.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think it will fulfil the benefit that Mr Kok and Mr Pritam Singh mentioned, using the existing channels that we have.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamed, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to take the opportunity to thank all Members for their cuts and making the COS for MCI a meaningful one for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I wish them every success in executing the Budget presented.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
